2_Introduction: The device achieved a remarkable PCE of 24.6984%, with a VOC of 1.1814 V, JSC of 26.32 mA/cm², and FF of 79.4301%. By preparing a base solution of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.65 mol/L, the perovskite precursor was ready for further enhancements. The precursor solution was deposited on the substrate and spun cast at 1000 rpm for 5 s, followed by 5500 rpm for 30 s. 150 µL CB as the antisolvent was dripped on the film at 15 s before the end of the last procedure. After spin-coating, the films were annealed on the hot plate at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The optimized crystallization of the mixed-cation Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3 perovskite, from a high-concentration 1.65 mol/L precursor, is directed by a precise spin-coating protocol where an initial 1000 rpm spread step ensures solution uniformity before the 5500 rpm acceleration phase, with the critical timing of chlorobenzene antisolvent dripping at 15 seconds before the end inducing rapid supersaturation and a high density of nucleation sites that suppress uncontrolled crystal growth and favor the formation of a compact, pinhole-free morphology with reduced grain boundaries, a process subsequently locked in by thermal annealing at 110°C for 15 minutes to drive full crystallization and mitigate intrinsic defect formation, ultimately yielding a high-quality photoactive layer where enhanced charge carrier lifetimes and suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways directly enable the remarkable photovoltaic parameters of a VOC of 1.1814 V, a JSC of 26.32 mA/cm², a FF of 79.4301%, and a champion PCE of 24.6984%.
